newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Egis expects exports to play a rising role.
newsitem.headline: Egis expects exports to play a rising role.

text.p: Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Egis Gyogyszergyar Rt said on Monday that it expected its exports to grow more rapidly in 1997 than domestic sales.
The company, which released its 1996 results on Friday, said it expected to boost its sales to around 30 billion forints in 1997 and plans to post a pre-tax profit of 6.3 billion.
"Within sales, exports will grow far more dynamically," Laszlo Marosffy, Egis's Deputy General Director told a news conference. "We plan to boost our exports by 14 percent (in 1997) in dollar terms."
In forint terms the company plans a 16 percent rise in domestic sales and a 33 percent increase in exports over 1996, when Egis's total sales amounted to 24.69 billion forints.
Even if Egis expects local sales to rise less rapidly than exports in 1997, it believes that the Hungarian market offers niches.
"We think that all leading Egis products have the potential for further market growth," Marosffy said.
In 1997 Egis plans to market 10 generic products and also three products from Servier, its majority owner, in Hungary.
In 1996 domestic sales accounted for 54.9 percent of Egis's total sales and this ratio will drop to 52 percent in 1997 and to below 50 percent in 1998, he said.
Marosffy said the company planned to invest some five billion forints in 1997 after investing 4.04 billion forints last year.
Roughly 70 percent of this amount will go for the completion of a new packaging unit this year and the reorganisation of the information system, Marosffy said.
Egis will also invest in raising the capital in each of its own companies in the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Poland, and in a majority-owned firm in Russia.
On Monday on the Budapest Stock Exchange Egis shares closed at 11,050 forints, up 650, after CS First Boston said it maintained its 'buy' rating on Egis shares.
